clue.text: Times indicates unusual influences

definitions.meaning: second meaning: magical charms cast over someone

explanation.surface: A newspaper reports that strange forces are at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper; it is a plain plural noun for stretches of time. 'Indicates' is itself a third sense, as in 'this spells trouble'.
explanation.definitionFit: A spell is both a stretch of time and an enchantment, a mysterious power working on someone.

clue.text: Confident doctor will take care of Prince or other leader

indicators.note: taking care of something means holding it safe, so one piece wraps around the royal one

parts.note: confident means certain
P is the standard abbreviation for prince
MO is a medical officer

explanation.surface: A self-assured physician looks after a royal patient or some other head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: The prince sits inside SURE, and the doctor follows. A prince is one leader, so the answer is the 'other' kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A supremo is a person in overall charge of an organisation, a boss or chief.

clue.text: Country, say, may stop it, finally

parts.note: e.g. means 'for example', which is what 'say' means here

indicators.note: finally applies to each of the preceding words, asking for the closing letter of each

parts.note: the final letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A nation might at last put an end to something.
explanation.definitionFit: Egypt is a nation in north-east Africa, so it is an instance of a country.

clue.text: Liberal, keeping working with copper, shows a bit of pride

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so the party word holds the next pieces inside it

parts.note: LIB is the short form of Liberal
a machine that is on is working
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A left-leaning politician who keeps working alongside the police shows some self-esteem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pride' looks like self-respect, but it is the collective noun for a group of lions.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of lions is called a pride, and a young lion is one small member of it.

clue.text: Hurried back, saving time, chasing American experts

indicators.note: what chases comes behind, so the American letter goes in front of the rest

parts.note: A is a standard abbreviation for American

indicators.note: saving something means keeping it inside, so the turned word holds the time letter
going back means travelling the other way, so the word for hurried is read from its end

parts.note: hurried means went fast
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Specialists from the US are pursued by someone rushing back to save a few minutes.
explanation.walkthrough: SPED turned round holds T, and the American comes in front because the rest is chasing it.
explanation.definitionFit: Adepts are people highly skilled in a field, which is what experts are.

clue.text: Try to get money from murderer, having seen off one classic murder victim

parts.note: to dun someone is to press them for payment of a debt

indicators.note: to see someone off is to get rid of them, so the numeral is removed from the killer

parts.note: Cain killed his brother Abel in Genesis
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone tries to blackmail a killer who has already disposed of one victim.
explanation.walkthrough: Cain loses his I. 'Classic' points to Shakespeare's Macbeth, where King Duncan is murdered.
explanation.definitionFit: King Duncan is murdered by Macbeth in Shakespeare's tragedy, the best-known killing in classic drama.

clue.text: Lively caper with bread for each person

indicators.note: something lively jumps about, so the letters of the frolic word are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
pita is a flat bread, also spelt pitta

explanation.surface: A jolly romp with sandwiches handed out to everybody.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase per capita literally means 'by heads', so for each individual.

clue.text: Long fish — what makes you see length?

parts.note: the letter S and the letters EE together make the word see
L is the abbreviation for length

explanation.surface: A puzzling question about a slender fish and what lets you judge distance.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'see' as a word to be spelt: the phrase S AND EE describes how it is built, then L is added.
explanation.definitionFit: The sand eel is a slim, elongated little fish that burrows in sand.

clue.text: Small recompense in America that's secured for striker

parts.note: a cent is a small coin, the hundredth of a US dollar, hence 'in America'

indicators.note: a thing secured is held fast inside something else, so the small word sits within the payment word

parts.note: a reward recompenses someone
taken as written

explanation.surface: A footballer is paid a pittance in the US.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striker' sounds like someone downing tools over low pay; in football it is the attacking player. 'In America' tells you the small coin is American.
explanation.definitionFit: In football the centre forward is the main attacking player, the team's chief goalscorer or striker.

clue.text: Supplier of distilleries certainly backing installing power

indicators.note: installing means putting something in place inside, so the power letter goes within
backing means moving backwards, so the word for certainly is read in reverse

parts.note: yes means certainly
P is the abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A whisky maker certainly supports putting in electricity.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spey is a Scottish river whose valley holds many whisky distilleries, which draw their water from it.
explanation.definitionFit: The River Spey feeds water to the many malt whisky distilleries of Speyside in Scotland.

clue.text: Marine area — you could get tan for once

indicators.note: the phrase says these letters could be made into something else, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: At the seaside you might, for a change, end up with a suntan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For once' reads as an idiom but is part of the letters to be reworked.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocean front is the stretch of land facing the sea, a seaside zone.

clue.text: Start of powerful big film about Troy, not gut-wrenching

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, which is all that is kept

parts.note: the opening letter

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the film word goes around the weight letter

parts.note: an epic is a grand-scale film
t is the abbreviation for troy, the weight system

explanation.surface: A mighty blockbuster about the Trojan War that isn't too harrowing.
explanation.walkthrough: Troy looks like the ancient city but is the weight system, abbreviated t. The definition is playful: peptic means digestive.
explanation.definitionFit: Peptic means relating to or aiding digestion, so it describes a stomach that is settled rather than churned.

clue.text: Studies collecting each source of currants for fruit buns

indicators.note: collecting means gathering up inside, so the word for studies holds the pieces

parts.note: to take a subject is to study it, so takes means studies

indicators.note: source of points at the first letter of currants

parts.note: first letter of currants

explanation.surface: Research collects each origin of the currants used in buns.
explanation.definitionFit: Teacakes are light sweet yeast buns containing dried fruit, usually toasted and buttered.

clue.text: Dish not for vegans? Criticise and grumble

parts.note: to roast someone is to criticise them harshly
a beef is a complaint

explanation.surface: A meat-eater's challenge: knock vegans and moan.
explanation.definitionFit: Roast beef is a meat dish, the British Sunday staple that no vegan would eat.

clue.text: Indulge prank about Northern river rising

indicators.note: about here means around, so the prank word wraps the compass letter

parts.note: a spoof is a hoax or trick
N is the abbreviation for northern

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means going upwards, so the river is read bottom to top

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain

explanation.surface: A practical joke involves a northern river in flood.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'rising' means read upwards, so the river goes in backwards at the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: To spoon-feed is to pamper someone by doing everything for them, so it means to indulge.

clue.text: Limited volume restricting one old instrument

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the shortened volume word encloses the numeral

parts.note: the word cut short to its usual abbreviation
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A quiet setting stops a single antique from being played loudly.
explanation.definitionFit: The viol was a bowed string instrument of the Renaissance and Baroque, ancestor-like cousin of the violin family.

clue.text: Recalled best place

indicators.note: recalled read as called back, so the word for best is read backwards

parts.note: tops means the best

explanation.surface: Someone remembers the finest location.
explanation.definitionFit: A spot is a particular location, so it is a synonym of place.

clue.text: Former Dutch colony almost certainly in America

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word for certainly loses its final letter

parts.note: sure means certainly
taken as written
Am is the abbreviation for America

explanation.surface: A one-time Dutch possession was probably in the Americas.
explanation.walkthrough: SURE loses its last letter. Surinam is an older spelling of Suriname, on the north coast of South America.
explanation.definitionFit: Surinam, now Suriname, was a Dutch colony in South America until independence in 1975.

clue.text: Atom lab also repeatedly involved with source of molecules

indicators.note: involved means tangled, so the letters are mixed up
repeatedly means the word also is written down twice
the source of molecules is its first letter

explanation.surface: A nuclear lab that repeatedly deals with molecules too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeatedly' gives ALSOALSO; 'involved' rearranges it with M from 'source of molecules'.
explanation.definitionFit: The New Mexico laboratory where the atomic bomb was developed is the archetypal atom lab.

clue.text: Former Communist state embargo, inter alia

indicators.note: inter is Latin for between or among, so the embargo word goes in the middle of the Latin word

parts.note: taken as written
an embargo is a ban on trade

explanation.surface: A trade ban was one of many measures against a Cold War regime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inter alia' is Latin for 'among other things'; split up, inter means between, so the ban goes inside ALIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Albania was a hardline Communist country in the Balkans until 1991.

clue.text: Inaccurate throw? One's excluded from team, perhaps

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read as two words: a cast that goes out of bounds
second meaning: a person rejected by a group

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is whimsical, splitting the word into 'out' and 'cast', a throw.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcast is someone shunned or rejected by society or a group, like a player left out of a side.

clue.text: Cockney fell — 'ow much was 'e carrying?

indicators.note: Cockney speakers drop the H sound at the start of words, so the opening letter goes

parts.note: fell as an adjective means cruel or deadly

explanation.surface: A Londoner took a tumble – how much was he holding?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fell' looks like the past tense of fall, but it is the old adjective meaning cruel. Cockneys (East Londoners) traditionally drop the H, as the definition's own spelling shows.
explanation.definitionFit: An armful is as much as a person can carry in their arms, answering how much was carried.

clue.text: Conclusion of printer in printing dispute? It offers a good view

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another, so the kept letter goes within the type word

parts.note: a font is a set of type for printing

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its closing letter, the only one kept

parts.note: the final letter
a row is a quarrel

explanation.surface: A print-shop strike ends; how would one watch it best?
explanation.definitionFit: The front row of seats in a theatre or stadium is closest to the action, giving the best sightline.

clue.text: Not the obvious way you progress initially into historic city

indicators.note: into means going inside, so the two letters are put within the city

parts.note: Bath is an English city famous for its Roman baths

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the two words before it

parts.note: the opening letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Take an unusual route when travelling into an old city.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath is a Georgian spa city in Somerset, south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A bypath is a side path or byway, a less frequented route rather than the main road.

clue.text: Ski-track confusion after stone buried

indicators.note: something buried lies hidden inside, so the weight abbreviation sits within the jumble word

parts.note: pie is a jumbled mess, as in printer's pie
st is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight of fourteen pounds

explanation.surface: Chaos on the slopes after a rock was covered over.
explanation.definitionFit: A piste is a prepared run of compacted snow for skiing, so a ski track.

clue.text: Viral treatment recalled irritation with hesitation — privy to containing that

indicators.note: containing means holding within, so the phrase for privy to wraps around the earlier pieces

parts.note: to be in on something is to be privy to it

indicators.note: recalled read as called back, so the irritation word is read backwards

parts.note: fret is worry or irritation
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: A cure for a virus is remembered with annoyance and doubt by someone in the know.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That' points back to the reversed word plus ER, which IN ON surrounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Interferon is a protein the body makes against viruses, also given as a drug for viral infections.

clue.text: Playwright's aphorism enthralling hearts

indicators.note: to enthral once meant to hold captive, so the saying holds the card letter inside

parts.note: a saw is an old saying
H is the card-game abbreviation for hearts

explanation.surface: A dramatist's witty saying captivates audiences.
explanation.definitionFit: George Bernard Shaw was the Irish dramatist who wrote Pygmalion and was famous for his aphorisms.

clue.text: Married cheat dashing first daughter's heart

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for married

indicators.note: dashing means knocking away, and first says which letter of the cheat word is struck

parts.note: to diddle is to swindle
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A wedded cheat breaks his first daughter's heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dashing first daughter' tells you to strike out the D at the front of the cheat word.
explanation.definitionFit: The heart of something is its centre, which is what the middle is.

clue.text: Hollow cheers reflected warning

parts.note: a cave is a hollow in rock

indicators.note: a reflection shows things back to front, so the word for cheers is read backwards

parts.note: ta is British slang for thank you, as is cheers

explanation.surface: Empty applause bounces back as a caution.
explanation.walkthrough: Ta and cheers are both informal British ways of saying thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: A caveat is a caution or proviso, a statement that warns of limits or conditions.
